- Rispetta la grafica dell'app originale
- Fai sì che posso integrare un AI o per ACP o per APi per chiedere consigli su codice committato o altro
- Togli tutti i riferimenti a GitKraken e trasformali in GitCerberoCraft
- Togli riferimenti a Trial, Premium e cose a pagamento

- Sei libero di aggiungere quello che ritieni opportuno che può servire a questa app"
Target: the program at C:\Users\Vinci\AppData\Local\gitkraken\gitkraken.exe
Your working folder is the project workspace (F:\Documents\GitCerberoCraft).

capture/README.md holds a first static look at the program (nothing was run) and, for a game, a list of its own files: maps, textures, models, sounds and settings. 1) Study the evidence, overview first (the README and summaries before the details). Where it leaves a gap that matters to the result, ask a focused follow-up with the craft-anything tools instead of guessing: capture another width or an opened state into a new folder under checks/, inspect a page or a bundle, look up a program's strings or functions by their exact names, read a game's settings or files. When it says another builder turn cannot resolve a comparison, stop retrying that comparison, keep it unverified and state the limit in your reply.

Set up another converter only for what these can't convert yet (such as models and sounds), and keep it inside the project folder. Never decrypt, crack or bypass encryption or copy protection: files inside encrypted archives (for example encrypted .pak, .utoc or .ucas files) stay closed. Recreate those as closely as you can from the pictures, the game's readable data and how it plays, in the same role, size, palette and feel, without reproducing logos or trademarks. List every original file you used in app/CREDITS.md with its source path, and start app/README.md with this line, as written: "This build contains the original game's own files, for the private use of the person who owns the game, on their own computer. It must not be shared or published." Craft Anything checks both after each build.

Keep it drawing while it isn't focused, or the picture never comes. In egui: `ViewportBuilder::with_active(false)`, on Windows `with_window_level(WindowLevel::AlwaysOnBottom)`, and on macOS `with_activate_ignoring_other_apps(false)` through `NativeOptions::event_loop_builder`; in Unity, `Application.runInBackground = true`; other stacks, their own way. Started without the option, the program opens as usual. Craft Anything runs it that way after each build to check the result, and a build without the option, or with a blank picture, doesn't pass. Try it yourself: run it with a file inside app/ (for example app/shots/now.png) and check that it saves the picture. Then open it with Read and look at it. "move": the player (or what they steer) moves; "act": their main action works (firing, mining, jumping, eating…); "hud": the on-screen information the original shows (score, health, ammo…) is drawn. ## craft-anything
Craft Anything shows how software works, with evidence. Start with core_investigation_show and core_session_show. Open a target with core_target_open (absolute path), then use focused tools; ask for summaries first and page for detail. Only the Essentials toolset is listed at first: call list_toolsets and enable_toolset to add native, Android, web and other tools. Keep the investigation memory current (core_brief_write, core_plan_update, core_hypothesis_record, core_finding_record with evidence ids, core_handoff_write at the end of each turn). Cite evidence ids, separate observations from inferences, and record open questions as unknowns. Tools that run code or change a device need the user's approval. In Clean room (Deep mode off) only the tools that work from outside are listed: nothing inside a target is read, and a refused tool says how to turn Deep mode on.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 28800000ms / 480 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 14400000ms (240 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. With `run_in_background` the timeout is instead how long the command may run in the background (default 14400000ms / 240 minutes, max 28800000ms / 8 hours); at that limit it is stopped and you are notified.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 28800000 for a foreground command)

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice.

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 14400000 ms, max 28800000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

data_uri.description: Data URI (-d), single-quoted for the device shell.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__adb_app_force_stop
tools.description: Force-stop a package with `am force-stop`. Changes the device.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__adb_app_install

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__adb_app_launch

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__adb_app_remove

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__adb_app_show

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__adb_apps_find
tools.description: Find installed packages whose name contains a search term with `pm list packages <query>`.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__adb_apps_list
tools.description: List installed package names with `pm list packages`. Scope all (default), third_party (-3) or system (-s).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__adb_bugreport_save

output_directory.description: Absolute host folder that must not exist yet; it is created fresh.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__adb_device_features_list
tools.description: List hardware and software features the device reports with `pm list features`.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__adb_device_show
tools.description: Read a whitelist of device properties with `getprop` (manufacturer, brand, model, Android version and SDK level, security patch, CPU ABIs, build fingerprint/type). The full property set is parsed and counted; a bounded sample is attached.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__adb_devices_find
tools.description: List phones and emulators attached to adb (`adb devices -l`): serial, connection state (device, unauthorized, offline...), product, model and transport id.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__adb_display_show
tools.description: Read display state with `dumpsys display`. Key lines (display ids, real size, density, state) are surfaced; a bounded raw tail is attached.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__adb_file_download
tools.description: Copy a file or folder from the device to a host folder with `adb pull`. output_directory must be absolute and fresh.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__adb_file_upload
tools.description: Copy a host file to the device with `adb push`. local_path is an absolute host file; device_path is an absolute device path. With overwrite=false the tool refuses if the device path already exists. Changes the device.

device_path.description: Absolute destination path on the device.

overwrite.description: Refuse if the device path already exists (default false → adb push overwrites).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__adb_folder_list
tools.description: List a folder on the device with `ls -la` (the path is single-quoted for the device shell). Raw lines are kept; a best-effort parse of name, size and permissions is attached.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__adb_log_read
tools.description: Read a bounded tail of the device log with `logcat -d` (dump and exit, never follow). count 1..10000 (default 500), buffer main|system|radio|events|crash (default main), optional pid filter. Lines are parsed into timestamp, pid, tid, level, tag and message.

pid.description: Only lines from this process id.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__adb_running_processes_list
tools.description: List running processes with `ps -A`, parsed into user, pid, ppid and name using the column header.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__adb_screenshot_take
tools.description: Take a screenshot with `exec-out screencap -p` and write screen.png to a fresh host folder. output_directory must be absolute and must not exist yet.

output_directory.description: Absolute host folder that must not exist yet; it is created fresh.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__adb_setting_get
tools.description: Read one settings value with `settings get <namespace> <key>`. namespace system|secure|global; key is validated.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__adb_system_services_list
tools.description: List registered system services with `service list`: index, name and the AIDL interface each exposes.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__adb_window_show
tools.description: Read window-manager state with `dumpsys window`. Focused window and app, and current activity lines are surfaced; a bounded raw tail is attached.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__ai_model_options_set
tools.description: Save a Copilot backend's context tier. Null inherits the CLI default. Refuses a stale expected_cli_model and leaves thinking unchanged; use ai_model_set for model and thinking choices.

context.description: Null inherits the CLI's context choice.

expected_cli_model.description: The backend's cli_model when these choices were loaded; null means the CLI default.

CliContext.description: A provider's context tier, not a guessed token count. Copilot reports each model's limits.

input_schema.description: Persistable choices, with the selected backend model captured to reject a stale picker.
input_schema.title: SetModelOptions

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__ai_model_options_show
tools.description: Discover the selected Copilot model's context tiers without sending a model prompt. Returns cli_model for the expected_cli_model guard when saving. Use ai_models_list for model and thinking choices.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__ai_model_set
tools.description: Save a configured coding agent's model and optional thinking depth, validated against that instance's current model catalogue. Omit model and thinking to use the agent's default; omit thinking to use the selected model's default. Unsupported selections are refused.

Effort.description:
Shared thinking levels for API backends and agent CLI variants, ordered least to most.
Claude maps unsupported levels down with [`Effort::within`]; OpenCode requires the exact
variant in its live catalogue. The `effort` and `cli_thinking` settings remain independent.

oneOf.description: Longer-horizon work than `high`.
The deepest reasoning, with no limit on tokens spent.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__ai_models_list
tools.description: List the visible chat models and supported thinking depths of a configured catalogue-capable coding agent. Uses the selected installation's configuration and credentials; only OpenCode supports SSH discovery. Returns a total and a page (offset, limit: default 200, maximum 1000). Discovery may start a process and update the CLI cache.

name.description: Configured backend name.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__android_app_graph_build
tools.description: Project an Android package's inventory (core_archive_show evidence or a path) into an application graph: manifest, DEX code, native libraries by ABI, split APKs, signing files, resources and embedded runtimes (Flutter, React Native/Hermes, Cordova/Capacitor, .NET, Unity...). Runtime hints are inferred from file names.

inventory.description: core_archive_show evidence (inline or retained). Its recorded path is re-read for the full inventory.

path.description: Or an absolute path to inventory now. Defaults to the active target when neither is given.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__android_class_show
tools.description: One class from an APK or .dex: superclass, interfaces, access flags, source file, annotations, fields and methods with Java-style signatures and overload indexes.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__android_class_users_find
tools.description: Every instruction in every DEX file of an APK that calls, reads, writes, creates, casts to or loads a class (or only calls one of its methods when method_name is given), with the calling method and code offset. Paged.

method_name.description: Only calls to methods with this name.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__android_classes_find
tools.description: Search the classes defined in an APK's DEX files (or a bare .dex) by name; an empty query lists every class. Paged (offset/limit).

path.description: Absolute path of the APK or .dex; the active target when omitted.

query.description: Case-insensitive part of a class name (dotted or descriptor form). Empty lists every class.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__android_components_list
tools.description: The activities, activity aliases, services, receivers and providers an APK's manifest declares: exported state and where it comes from, permissions, intent filters (actions, categories, data), and a plain reachable_from_outside flag with who_can_reach (any_app, apps_with_permission or own_app_only), following the manifest's implicit export rules for its targetSdk. Filter by kind or reachable_only; paged. Reads the manifest only; components an app registers while running aren't in it.

kind.description: Only this kind: activity, activity-alias, service, receiver or provider.

path.description: Absolute path of the APK; the active target when omitted.

reachable_only.description: Only components other apps can reach.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__android_dart_snapshot_show
tools.description: Read a Flutter app's compiled Dart library (libapp.so, from an APK or directly): the dynamic symbols for the VM and isolate snapshots (from section headers or, for stripped images, PT_DYNAMIC with DT_HASH/DT_GNU_HASH), snapshot headers (kind, version hash, features), and a byte scan of the isolate snapshot for package:/dart: URIs and identifier tokens (tokens paged with offset/limit).

abi.description: ABI folder to read from an APK (e.g. arm64-v8a); by default arm64-v8a, x86_64, x86, then armeabi-v7a.

offset.description: First identifier token of the page.

path.description: Absolute path of an APK or a libapp.so; the active target when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__android_flutter_identify
tools.description: For an APK (or one Flutter library): which ABIs ship libapp.so/libflutter.so, the Dart snapshot version hash (null with candidates when libraries disagree), Dart versions and toolchains the binaries state, GNU build ids, and the size and SHA-256 of each libflutter.so. Built-in parser.

path.description: Absolute path of an APK (or a libapp.so / libflutter.so); the active target when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__android_jeb_decompile
tools.description: Ask JEB to decompile one type or method (upstream decompile_code_item) by item_address, optionally inside unit_path. The output is JEB's, recorded as external evidence.

item_address.description: The item's address in JEB's notation, e.g. `Lcom/example/Main;` or `Lcom/example/Main;->onCreate(Landroid/os/Bundle;)V`.

timeout_secs.description: Seconds to wait for the whole exchange (1..=600).

unit_path.description: The code unit holding the item; JEB's default when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__android_jeb_open
tools.description: Ask the user-run JEB MCP server to open an absolute file path as a project (upstream open_project). Not idempotent: JEB keeps the project open.

path.description: Absolute path of the file to open in JEB (APK, DEX, ...).

timeout_secs.description: Seconds to wait for the whole exchange (1..=600).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__android_jeb_units_browse
tools.description: List the units of the open JEB project (upstream list_units), optionally under parent_unit_path and filtered, one page at a time (index, count ≤ 100).

filter.description: Only units whose name or path matches this text.

parent_unit_path.description: List the children of this unit instead of the project's top-level units.

timeout_secs.description: Seconds to wait for the whole exchange (1..=600).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__android_method_show
tools.description: A method's Dalvik bytecode as a smali-like listing with registers, resolved strings, types, fields and methods, branch targets, switch and array payloads and try/catch handlers (built-in decoder). With java_source=true and JADX installed, also attaches JADX's Java decompilation of the class.

java_source.description: Also ask JADX (if installed) for Java source of the class. Default false.

overload_index.description: Which overload (0-based, in declaration order) when the name is overloaded; 0 when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__android_package_show
tools.description: Read an APK with built-in parsers: the manifest (package, versions, SDK levels, permissions, components with exported state and intent filters, application flags) decoded from binary XML, signing certificates (v1 PKCS#7 files and the v2/v3 signing block; signatures and content digests are verified, but not whether the certificate is one you trust), DEX files and native libraries per ABI.

include_manifest_xml.description: Include the decoded manifest as XML text (default true).

path.description: Absolute path of the APK; the active target when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__android_resources_read
tools.description: Decode resources.arsc with the built-in parser: packages, resource types and their configurations (locale, density, night mode, SDK...), every entry with typed values and style bags, string resources per locale; optionally decode compiled res/*.xml files to text. Paged.

locale.description: Only this locale (`fr`, `es-rMX`; `default` for the unqualified one).

only_locales.description: Only these locales, each with its own string table (`["de", "fr", "default"]`); adds to `locale`.

path.description: Absolute path of the APK or a resources.arsc file; the active target when omitted.

type_name.description: Only entries of this resource type (`string`, `color`, `style`...).

with_strings.description: Include string resources grouped by locale (default true).

xml_files.description: Compiled XML files inside the APK to decode to text (e.g. `res/layout/main.xml`), at most 16.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__app_builds_line_up
tools.description: Pair the functions of two builds of a program (two absolute paths) with the built-in engine. In order: unique names that aren't generated; Rust names with the compiler's hashes left out (a crate's hash changes with the toolchain); identical bytes; bytes with addresses masked out; a structural fingerprint of block count, called names and referenced strings. Each pair says how it was matched, with what confidence, and what comparing the bodies found: a pair by name is still reported as changed when its code differs. Candidates that can't be told apart stay unpaired and are listed as ambiguous. Lists are paged together (offset/limit); show picks one; detail=summary keeps every row for core_evidence_browse. Nothing is executed. Takes as long as analysing both programs.

detail.description: complete (default) returns the page; summary keeps every row for core_evidence_browse.

left.description: Absolute path of the first (older) build.

max_file_bytes.description: Refuse files bigger than this (up to 2 GiB, default 512 MiB).

right.description: Absolute path of the second (newer) build.

show.description: all (default), pairs, changed (pairs whose code differs), ambiguous, only_left or only_right.

Detail.description:
The uniform summary-first detail control (see the module docs). `complete` is the default and
returns the full evidence record; `summary` returns a compact, pageable view.

MatchShow.description: Which list of a match to return.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__app_call_path_find
tools.description: Find a path of calls from a start address to a goal address over a call graph assembled from native_function_study evidence records for the same input binary.

functions.description: native_function_study evidence records from the same input binary, describing its functions and callees.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__app_changes_summarize
tools.description: Combine several comparison evidence records (app_function_versions_compare, core_archives_compare, runtime_captures_compare) into one summary of what changed and what stayed the same.

comparisons.description:
One or more comparison evidence records (app_function_versions_compare / core_archives_compare /
runtime_captures_compare / core_evidence_exports_compare), inline or by reference.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__app_coverage_evaluate
tools.description: Summarise a rebuild ledger: the share of in-scope expectations proven, counts by layer and status, and the open gaps with what each still needs.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__app_feature_follow
tools.description: Follow a feature through an application graph from a seed (module, function, string, IPC channel, endpoint, route, bridge API or node id): what leads to it and what it leads to, across renderer ↔ preload ↔ main, with readable chains and a one-line story.

application.description: js_app_map evidence (inline or {"kind":"saved","evidence_id":...}) or an absolute path to analyse.

oneOf.description: What the seed leads to.
What leads to the seed.
Case-insensitive substring.

value.description: What to look for: a channel name, function name, string, module path, URL fragment or node id.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__app_folder_explain
tools.description: Survey an installed app's folder (absolute path; a macOS .app or its Contents, a Windows or Linux install folder) when you don't know what it is. Walks the folder within max_entries and max_depth, following no links, running nothing and writing nothing, and reads only the first and last 4 KiB of the files that need a look, plus a search of up to 64 MiB of up to 4 main programs for Tauri's own text, to name the runtimes it may be built on: Electron, Tauri, CEF, Qt, Flutter, .NET, Java, Python (with PyInstaller), Node, Unity, Unreal, Godot, other game engines, or plain native code. Each candidate has a strength and the files that support it, and next_steps says which tool to run on which file. These are inferences: a file being there doesn't prove the app runs it.

max_depth.description: How many folders deep to look (up to 32).

max_entries.description: Most files and folders to look at (up to 200000).

path.description: Absolute path of the installed app's folder.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__app_function_versions_compare
tools.description: Compare two native_function_study evidence records: name, size, blocks, instructions, callee set and pseudo-code. Reports what changed.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__app_graphs_compare
tools.description: Compare two application graphs: modules (unchanged, changed, moved by content, renamed by structure, added, removed), bundle modules (content → structure → id), IPC channels and handlers, bridge members, endpoints, routes, window webPreferences, native modules and vendor versions.

left.description: The older version: js_app_map evidence or an absolute path.

right.description: The newer version, in the same forms.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__app_ledger_build
tools.description: Derive the expectations a clean-room rebuild must meet from an application graph (IPC handlers, bridge members, windows, endpoints, routes, storage, file/process effects, native modules, entry point) and mark each one proven only when the manifest gives it one owner, a parser type where needed, every case it must cover with strong enough evidence, and a passing check with its result. Ledger status: ready, open, failing or unclear.

application.description: js_app_map evidence or an absolute path to analyse.

manifest.description: How the rebuild binds expectations to owners, cases and verifiers.

reviewed_expectations.description: Expectations reviewed as out of scope or blocked.
