offset.description: First output line of the page.

path.description: Absolute path of the file; the active target when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_rizin_session_begin
tools.description: Start Rizin's debugger (user settings and scripts off, no prompt or colours) on a program (absolute path, optional arguments), which it starts stopped before its first instruction, or attach it to a running process by pid. Returns a session_id for native_rizin_session_command_run, native_rizin_session_show and native_rizin_session_end, plus Rizin's start-up messages. The program's own console output isn't captured. Sessions live in memory for this run; at most 4 at a time. Starting a program or attaching to one asks for consent.

pid.description: A running process to attach to instead of starting a program.

program.description: Absolute path of the program to start under the debugger.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_rizin_session_command_run
tools.description: Run one Rizin command line in a debug session (for example `dr` registers, `db main` breakpoint, `dc` continue, `ds` step, `dbt` backtrace, `dm` memory maps, `pd 10 @ rip`, `px 64 @ rsp`; chain with `;`) and return its output and any `ERROR:` lines, waiting up to timeout_seconds. A command still running at the deadline (a `dc` that never stops) keeps running and the next command waits for it. Visual mode isn't available. Commands can run the program and change its memory, so this asks for consent.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the command to finish: 1–300, default 10.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_rizin_session_end
tools.description: End a Rizin debug session: ask Rizin to quit (which ends a program it started; an attached process is detached), then stop it and anything it started.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_rizin_session_show
tools.description: Show one Rizin debug session (or all when session_id is omitted): whether Rizin is alive, what it debugs, whether a command is still running, and any output that arrived since the last command.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_rust_binary_show
tools.description: Identify a Rust program (ELF, PE or Mach-O, or any file) from its bytes: rustc version strings and the toolchain commit from /rustc/<commit>/ paths, the standard-library path layout, crates with versions from embedded Cargo paths (registry/src/<index>/<crate>-<version>/ and git checkouts), the program's own source paths left by panic locations, well-known panic messages, Rust symbol names (legacy and v0 mangling) with demangled samples and whether they are stripped, and the cargo-auditable dependency list (.dep-v0) when present. Confidence is honest: strong signals (symbols, toolchain paths, dependency data) versus weak ones (panic text alone). Built-in; never runs the program.

path.description: Absolute path of the program; the active target when omitted.

Detail.description:
The uniform summary-first detail control (see the module docs). `complete` is the default and
returns the full evidence record; `summary` returns a compact, pageable view.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_sections_list
tools.description: Segments and sections with address ranges, file offsets, permissions and entropy.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_source_folder_write
tools.description: Write each function of the active target as pseudo-C to its own file in a folder, across as many runs as it takes: running again with the same folder skips what's done and continues, and a state file records the target's SHA-256 (another target is refused) and each finished function. Each call stops at max_functions or max_seconds and says how far it got. Files are written atomically. Uses the built-in decompiler, as native_functions_decompile does. Refuses a folder with other files in it.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

folder.description: Absolute path of the folder to write to: new or empty, or one an earlier run of this tool wrote.

max_functions.description: Most functions to write in this call (1..=1000000, default 1000).

max_seconds.description: Stop starting new functions after this long (0..=3600, default 120).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_strings_browse
tools.description: Printable strings (ASCII, UTF-8, UTF-16) in data sections with their addresses and how many places use them. Optional filters: one address, one section (`.rdata`); native_strings_find finds text. Paged.

address.description: Only the string at this address (0x-hex).

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

section.description: Only strings in this section (`.rdata`, `__cstring`; case doesn't matter).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_strings_find
tools.description: Complete, deterministic search of the program's strings. mode literal or regex; case-insensitive unless case_sensitive. Paged.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_value_flow_show
tools.description: Register def-use graph of a function (which instruction's result each instruction reads), parameter uses and side effects, following callees to max_depth. Nodes are paged (offset/limit).

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

function.description: Function name or address.

max_call_sites.description: Most call sites to examine (1..=4096, default 256).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_window_capture
tools.description: Start a program (an app or a game), wait for its window, take a picture of it and close the program (Windows and macOS). Optionally save the PNG to `output`, and the UI tree of its windows (as runtime_ui_read reads it; Windows and macOS) to `ui_tree` as JSON. It runs the program, so it needs consent.

output.description: Save the picture here as a PNG (an absolute path; its folder must exist).

program.description: The program to start (an absolute path).

ui_tree.description:
Also save the UI tree of its windows here as JSON, read just before it's closed (an
absolute path; its folder must exist). Windows and macOS.

wait_secs.description: Seconds to let it start and draw before the picture (default 8, at most 120).

working_directory.description: Working folder for the program (an absolute directory). Defaults to its executable's folder.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_xrefs_list
tools.description: References to an address (calls, jumps, data, strings, pointers, imports) and the references made from it. Defaults to the cursor. Paged.

document.description: Open target (document) to use; the active one when omitted.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__packets_capture_show
tools.description: Summarize a saved pcap or pcapng capture with the built-in decoder (nothing installed): format, interfaces and link types, packet and byte counts, time span, frames per protocol, busiest addresses, conversations (flows) with packets and bytes in each direction and the application protocols seen (paged), DNS questions and answers, HTTP/1.x requests (method, Host, target; credentials removed) and TLS ClientHello server names (SNI) and ALPN. Decodes Ethernet (VLAN), raw IP, Linux cooked and loopback links; IPv4, IPv6, TCP, UDP, ICMP. Each packet is decoded on its own: no stream reassembly, no decryption.

limit.description: Conversations per page (1–5000, default 100). Inventories show their top 100.

path.description: Absolute path of a .pcap/.pcapng file; the active target when omitted.

Detail.description:
The uniform summary-first detail control (see the module docs). `complete` is the default and
returns the full evidence record; `summary` returns a compact, pageable view.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__packets_fields_show
tools.description: List decoded fields of individual packets in a saved pcap or pcapng capture, paged: frame number, time, link, protocol stack, addresses and ports, conversation (flow) id, IP TTL, TCP flags/sequence/window, UDP and ICMP details, DNS questions and answers, HTTP/1.x request or status line with Host, TLS ClientHello SNI/ALPN/versions. Filter by protocol (e.g. dns, tls, http, tcp, udp, icmp, ipv6, arp), IP address, port, or flow id from packets_capture_show. Built-in decoder.

flow.description: Only packets of this conversation (the flow id from packets_capture_show, e.g. 3 or "f3").

ip.description: Only packets from or to this IP address.

offset.description: First matching packet of the page.

path.description: Absolute path of a .pcap/.pcapng file; the active target when omitted.

port.description: Only packets from or to this TCP/UDP port.

protocol.description: Only packets with this protocol in their stack (eth, vlan, ipv4, ipv6, arp, tcp, udp, icmp, icmpv6, dns, mdns, http, tls).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__packets_inventory_show
tools.description: Inventories of a saved pcap or pcapng capture: packet count, protocol stacks, IPv4/IPv6 addresses with packet counts, DNS questions and the addresses answered for them, TLS server names (SNI) and HTTP request URIs (credentials removed), each with counts and limited to `limit` rows. Uses Wireshark's tshark when installed (engine=auto or tshark; full dissectors, run with a deadline and capped output) and the built-in decoder otherwise (engine=built_in forces it).

limit.description: Rows kept per inventory, most frequent first (1–10000, default 100).

path.description: Absolute path of a .pcap/.pcapng file; the active target when omitted.

oneOf.description: tshark when installed, the built-in decoder otherwise.

Detail.description:
The uniform summary-first detail control (see the module docs). `complete` is the default and
returns the full evidence record; `summary` returns a compact, pageable view.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__plugins_add
tools.description: Add an external MCP server as a plugin ([[plugins.mcp]] in config.toml): an id, and either a command (a local server, with args, env and cwd) or a url (a remote https server, with headers). A plugin added here always asks before each call. replace overwrites a plugin with the same id. Run plugins_refresh next to read its tools.

command.description: The program of a local server.

headers.description: Sent with every request to a remote server (e.g. `Authorization`).

id.description: Toolset id and tool-id prefix: lower-case letters, digits and `_`.

name.description: The name people see (default: the id).

replace.description: Overwrite a plugin with the same id.

url.description: A remote server's address: `https://...`, or `http://` to this computer.

wasm.description:
A WASM component plugin's file (full path to a `.wasm`), instead of a command or url. Its
tools load from the next start, in a build with the `wasm-plugins` feature.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__plugins_list
tools.description: The external MCP servers configured as plugins ([[plugins.mcp]] in config.toml): id, command, whether it's on and asks before each call, and the tools cached from its last refresh.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__plugins_refresh
tools.description: Start a plugin's MCP server (or every enabled one), read its tool list and cache it. New or changed tools are offered from the next start of the app or CLI. It runs the plugin's program, so it needs consent.

id.description: One plugin's id (default: every enabled plugin).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__plugins_remove
tools.description: Remove a plugin from config.toml by its id. Its tools stop being offered from the next start.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_approvals_set
tools.description: Choose, for one kind of builder action in a project, whether it goes ahead (`allow`), waits for the person's OK on a card (`ask`) or is refused (`refuse`); `default` follows Auto mode. Kinds: `web` (reading websites, searching), `commands` (outside the usual build commands), `outside_files` (changing files outside the project), `publish` (git push, npm publish, gh pr create...), `delete_outside`, `system` (system changes and files, Craft Anything's own records), `other_tools`. With no kind, says what every kind gets now. Takes effect from the builder's next action, also mid-build. Only the person changes these: an agent's call may only make a kind stricter.

kind.description: The kind of action (`publish`, `web`...); none just reads what every kind gets.

ActionKind.description:
A kind of builder action that asks for approval, which a project can decide about ahead of time
(`Manifest::approvals`).

oneOf.description: Reading websites and searching the web.
Commands outside the usual build commands.
Changing files outside the project.
Pushing to a git server or publishing anywhere (`git push`, `npm publish`, `gh pr create`...).
Deleting anything outside the project or the temp folder.
Changing the system, its settings or users, system files, or Craft Anything's own records.
Tools with no rule of their own.

ApprovalChoice.description: What one kind of a project's builder actions should get.

oneOf.description: What Auto mode gives it.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_assets_allow
tools.description: Turn on or off whether the builder may generate pictures and 3D models for a project (paid per asset from its asset budget, and only with an asset provider's key), or read it with no value. Off until the person turns it on.

allow.description: true lets the builder generate assets, false stops it; leave out to only read it.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_assets_budget
tools.description: Set what a project may spend on generated pictures and 3D models (US dollars), or read it with no amount. Shows what's been spent so far.

budget_usd.description: The new budget in US dollars (0 to 10 000); leave out to only read it.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_build_finish
tools.description: The person is happy with the build as it is (#210): its status becomes Ready and the conversation says they called it done, so a paused, stopped or failed build no longer offers to carry on. Everything so far is kept, and a new message carries on from here. It doesn't stop a build that is still running: pause it first.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_delete
tools.description: Delete a project: everything Craft Anything made in its folder (its records, checks, and what was built in app/). The person's own files stay (an app edited in place, the files a project started from). Can't be undone, so `confirm` must be true; stop a build first.

confirm.description: Must be true: deleting can't be undone.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_duplicate
tools.description: Copy a project beside it under a new name, to try something else from where it is: what was built, the pictures of the original and the study come along; the conversation, questions and usage don't, and neither do dependencies or compiler output (the next build makes them again). An app edited in place is copied into the copy's app/ folder.

name.description: The copy's name (default: "<name> copy").

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_inbox_answer
tools.description: Answer a question or approval a project is waiting on (an id from project_show): a choice or text for questions, allow (and always) for approvals. The answer reaches a running build at once and is kept in the project's conversation.

always.description: Allow this kind of action for the rest of the project (approvals).

text.description: A typed answer (questions), or a reason (approvals).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_list
tools.description: List the projects in every project folder from settings (where new projects go, then `project_folders`), or in one folder, newest first: name, folder, app folder, request, target, stack, status, the latest check and how many questions are waiting.

projects_dir.description: Only this folder (default: every project folder from settings).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_open_folder
tools.description: Open the project's folder (or its app/ folder) in the file manager, or one of its pinned builds' folders.

app.description: Open the app/ folder (what was built) instead of the project folder.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_pin_create
tools.description: Keep the project's current build at hand to open later, whatever the builder changes next. `frozen` (the default) copies the app's files and its program into the project's pinned/ folder, without compiler output or dependencies it doesn't start from, so rebuilds can't change or break it. `light` copies the program and the code too but hard-links dependencies and media to the project's, saving their space: replacing or deleting those in the project leaves the pin's as they were, but a file rewritten in place changes in both. With `estimate`, only says what each would take. Websites can't be pinned yet.

estimate.description: Only say what each kind of copy would take; pin nothing.

mode.description:
`frozen` (default): a copy of its own; `light`: shares dependencies and media with the
project. `live` was retired and is refused.

name.description: Its name (default: the project's name and round).

PinMode.description: How a pin keeps its build.

oneOf.description: Its own copy of the build, which nothing else changes (the default).
Its own program and code, sharing dependencies and media with the project.

The project's app where it is, as the latest build left it. No longer made (it only
opened what Play opens); pins already saved this way still work.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_pin_delete
tools.description: Remove a pin. Its copy goes with it, including anything the program saved beside itself there, so `confirm` must be true; a running pin is refused until it's stopped.

confirm.description: Must be true: a pin's copy, and what it saved, can't be brought back.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_pin_open
tools.description: Start a pinned build in its own window. If it's already running, says so instead of starting a second copy, unless `another` is true (copies of one pin share the files they save beside themselves). A start that quits within two seconds is reported with its exit code and last output. It runs the code the builder wrote, so it needs the person's consent.

another.description: Start another copy even if one is running.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_pin_rename
tools.description: Give a pin a new name.

name.description: Its new name.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_pin_stop
tools.description: Close what a pin started in this session (every copy of it).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_pins_list
tools.description: The pins of one project, or of every project in the project folders from settings: id, name, frozen or light, the round it was pinned at, its size, and whether it's running (started in this session).

project.description: Only this project's pins (default: every project's).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_plan_fold
tools.description: Fold the builder's plan card away (#504). The steps stay in the project's conversation, and a later run's plan shows again. Call it between builds: a build saves its conversation as it goes, so a fold made during one can be overwritten by that build's next save.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_play
tools.description: Start the finished game or app a project built (its program, a Unity or Unreal package, or a Godot project in Godot), in its own window. If it's already running, says so instead of starting a second copy, unless `another` is true. A start that quits within two seconds is reported with its exit code and last output. It runs the code the builder wrote, so it needs the person's consent. Websites use project_preview instead. Known limit on Windows: when the caller's output is a pipe, the started program inherits it, so a caller reading that output to its end waits until the program exits (#207).

another.description: Start another copy even if one is running.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_preview
tools.description: Serve a project's built website on this computer only (loopback) and return its address. It keeps serving for this session; with `wait`, the call itself serves until it's cancelled (Ctrl+C in the CLI).

wait.description: Serve until the call is cancelled instead of returning at once (for the CLI).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_questions_set
tools.description: Choose whether the builder's questions (core_person_ask) in a project are shown to the person to answer (`ask`) or answered with "decide yourself and say what you chose" (`decide`); `default` follows the app's setting (`questions` in settings, which follows Auto mode until set). With no mode, says what applies now. Takes effect from the builder's next question, also mid-build.

mode.description: `ask`, `decide` or `default`; none just reads what applies.

QuestionsChoice.description: What a project's questions should get.

oneOf.description: The app's setting.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_rename
tools.description: Give a project a new name (its folder stays where it is).

name.description: Its new name.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__project_show
tools.description: One project: its request, target, stack, status, checks, questions still waiting for an answer, and its conversation (paged with offset/limit, newest last).

limit.description: Return at most this many items (default and maximum 200; the newest when no offset).

offset.description: Skip this many conversation items from the start.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__radio_decoders_list
tools.description: List the device protocols the installed rtl_433 can decode: number, name, and whether it runs by default (the others only run when asked for with decoders). Optional engine.

filter.description: Only decoders whose name contains this text (any case).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__radio_recording_decode
tools.description: Decode a saved radio recording (absolute path or the active target) with rtl_433: I/Q samples (.cu8, .cs8, .cs16, .cf32) or demodulated AM/FM (.am.s16, .fm.s16), format and sample rate read from the file name (for example g001_433.92M_250k.cu8; 250 kHz when absent) unless sample_rate is given. Returns each decoded message (device model, id, channel and readings) paged with offset/limit, plus counts by model. decoders limits decoding to those protocol numbers (see radio_decoders_list); otherwise rtl_433's default set runs. Optional engine.

decoders.description: Protocol numbers to decode (from radio_decoders_list); empty runs the default set.

path.description: Absolute path of the recording; omit to use the active target.

sample_rate.description: Sample rate in Hz, when the file name doesn't say.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__rebuild_activity_show
tools.description: What a project's builds did, line by line, newest last: each stage, every command and file the builder touched and how it ended, what it said, and what programs printed outside the conversation. Secrets are hidden. Works while a build runs and after. `limit` lines (200 by default, at most 2000), `offset` lines back from the newest.

limit.description: How many lines to return (200 by default, at most 2000).

offset.description: How many lines back from the newest to end at (0 by default).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__rebuild_check
tools.description: For the builder: test the project's current build against the original now, with the same checks Craft Anything runs after each turn (a website's likeness at each width with the padding, colour, font and layout differences; an app's or game's picture against the original's; whether it builds; the mechanics sheet; credits). The project's running build answers it, so the builder can fix what it lists and check again before replying. Not counted as a round. project defaults to the project this tool server works for.

project.description: The project's folder; default: the project this tool server was started for.

wait_minutes.description:
Longest wait for the result, in minutes (1..=60, default 35): a website with several pages
or a game's engine build takes a few minutes, and the run stops a check at 30.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__rebuild_note
tools.description: Tell a running build something more; the agent reads it at its next step. With no build running, start a follow-up with rebuild_start instead.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__rebuild_note_withdraw
tools.description: Take back a note given with rebuild_note (by the id it returned) while the agent hasn't read it yet; it returns the note's text. Once the agent has read it, it can't be taken back.

id.description: The note's id, as rebuild_note returned it.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__rebuild_question_ask
tools.description: Ask a question about a project's build ("where are the latest files?", "why this engine?") without starting a build or a round, and without changing anything. Claude Code answers from a copy of the builder's own session, which isn't kept, reading files only (none in Clean room); an AI with an API key answers with the tools that change nothing. Other coding agents are refused. Safe while a build runs: it doesn't interrupt it. Returns the answer, how it was answered and its cost, and keeps it in the project (`rebuild_questions_list`).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__rebuild_questions_list
tools.description: The questions asked about a project's build and their answers, oldest first (the newest 200).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__rebuild_start
tools.description: Start building: a new project from a request and a target (a web address, an absolute path, or - for none), or a follow-up on an existing project. A coding agent studies, builds, checks and refines in the background; follow it with rebuild_status and project_show, answer its questions with project_inbox_answer. Up to `build.parallel` projects build at once (2 by default); more are queued and start on their own as others finish. It runs a coding agent that writes and builds code, so it needs consent.

backend.description:
The coding agent to use (an enabled backend name), kept with a new project for its later
changes; default: the one set up for building.

build_with.description: What to build with: an engine (unity, unreal, godot, rust) or a stack's full name.

existing.description:
With `project_folder` that has files and isn't a project yet: `edit` (they're the app,
edited in place) or `start_from` (material to start from; the app is built in app/ beside
them).

generate_assets.description:
For a new game: the builder may generate pictures and 3D models (paid from the person's
asset provider key, within the project's budget). Default false; change it later with
project_assets_allow.

pictures.description:
Pictures of the original (absolute paths): the look the person expects. They're copied
into the project's reference/ folder for the builder.

project.description: Continue this project folder instead of starting a new one.

project_folder.description:
Start the new project in this folder itself instead (it's added to the project list). If
it already has files, `existing` says what they are; if it already holds a project, its
saved target, settings and stack are kept and `request` becomes its follow-up.

projects_dir.description: Where a new project's folder goes (default: the projects folder from settings).

request.description:
What to make (a new project), or the follow-up message (with `project`, or a
`project_folder` that already holds one).

resume.description:
With `project`: carry on where its last run stopped (paused, or the app or the computer
stopped) instead of sending `request` as a follow-up.

rounds.description: Refinement rounds after the first build (default 2).

target.description:
For a new project: a web address, an absolute path to an app, game or file, or `-` for none.
A `project_folder` that already holds one keeps its saved target.

ExistingFiles.description: What the files already in a picked folder are to a new project.

oneOf.description: The app itself: the builder edits them in place.
Material to start from: the builder reads them and builds the app in app/ beside them.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__rebuild_status
tools.description: Whether a project's build is running in this session (or queued, and where), its status and note, the latest check, and how many questions are waiting.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__rebuild_stop
tools.description: Pause a project's running build. Its work so far is kept; a follow-up continues it.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__runtime_captures_compare
tools.description: Compare two runtime_walkthrough_record evidence records dimension by dimension (terminal, exit, filesystem, events) and report what changed. Pure; no program is run.

left.description: The first run: runtime_walkthrough_record evidence (inline, {"kind":"saved",...} or a bare id).

right.description: The second run, in the same forms.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__runtime_ui_read
tools.description: Read the UI tree of a running app by its pid: every window's controls in order with their depth, role, title, identifier and value (macOS: the accessibility tree, optionally with a screenshot; Windows: UI Automation, also the class, position and size, and whether it's enabled; window_id picks one window by its handle). Password fields' values are never read; long values are cut at 500 characters. Other hosts get a clear wrong_os result.

max_nodes.description: Largest number of accessibility nodes to return.

pid.description: The process id of the running app.

screenshot.description:
Include a screenshot (PNG, base64) alongside the tree. macOS 14+: captures one on-screen
window belonging to pid, restricted by window_id when supplied, at up to 2048 pixels
per side. Without window_id, captures the first matching window. Needs existing Screen
Recording permission; failures are explicit limitations and never open permission dialogs.

window_id.description: A specific window to restrict to (on Windows, its window handle).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__runtime_ui_walkthrough_record
tools.description: Run a short scripted UI walkthrough against a running app by its pid and record its UI tree before and after the steps. Each step names an action and an element (its exact title or identifier). macOS: any accessibility action (e.g. AXPress). Windows (UI Automation): press (invoke, else toggle, select or expand), expand, collapse, toggle, select or focus; AXPress, AXShowMenu and AXRaise work too. Each step reports dispatched, element_not_found, not_supported, unknown_action or failed. Password fields' titles and values are never read. Other hosts get wrong_os.

steps.description: Steps to perform, each an accessibility action such as press/focus on an element path.

action.description:
Accessibility action, e.g. `AXPress` (on Windows also press, expand, collapse, toggle,
select or focus).

element.description: Identifier or title path to the element the action targets.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__runtime_walkthrough_record
tools.description: Run a program under a terminal with a scripted timeline of typed input, resizes and signals, then record the terminal screen, exit, and (opt-in) which files changed. Values that change every run (process ids, loopback ports, 10 ms time buckets; optionally paths and literal patterns) are normalised so two runs compare. Bounded by time, output and files; the whole process group is killed on timeout or cancel. Runs code, so it needs your OK.

environment.description: Extra environment variables applied on top of the inherited environment.

executable.description: The program to run (absolute path or a name resolved on PATH).

finish_ms.description: 0 = SIGKILL at the deadline; > 0 = SIGTERM, wait this long, then SIGKILL.

normalization.description:
Make two runs comparable: replace values that change every run (on by default for process
ids, ports and 10 ms time buckets).

sandbox.description: Run inside bubblewrap if it is installed (recorded honestly either way).

watched_paths.description:
Absolute paths to snapshot before and after (opt-in). File contents are never read; only
path, size and sha256.

working_directory.description: Working directory (absolute). Defaults to the program's own default.

data.description: Text to type. A trailing newline is not added for you.

paths.description: Replace the working directory and the temp folder with <cwd> and <tmp>.

patterns.description: Literal replacements (no patterns), applied last; at most 100.

pids.description: Replace the run's process ids with <pid>.

ports.description: Replace ports after localhost, 127.0.0.1, 0.0.0.0 and [::1] with <port>.

time_step_ms.description: Round event dispatch times down to this many milliseconds (0 keeps them exact).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__settings_set
tools.description: Set one setting by its dotted key from settings_show (`auto_mode`, `deep_mode`, `projects_dir`, `assets.budget_usd`...) to a JSON value, then save. Unknown keys and values of the wrong type are refused, and nothing is written.

key.description: A dotted key from settings_show, e.g. `deep_mode`.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__settings_show
tools.description: The current settings as JSON (mode, Auto mode, Deep mode/Ghidra, engine paths, projects folder, asset budget and picture model, AI backends). API keys are never in settings.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__setup_apply
tools.description: Connect Craft Anything to coding-agent apps: register its MCP server in their config files (backing each up first) and install the skill. Changes other apps' files, so it asks first.

all_detected.description: Every agent app found on this computer.

clients.description: Client ids to set up (claude_code, codex, cursor...); empty refreshes the ones already set up.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__setup_doctor
tools.description: Check the install, each agent app's registration, engines, and that the MCP server answers.

clients.description: Only these clients; empty checks every detected one.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__setup_plan
tools.description: What connecting Craft Anything to coding-agent apps (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor...) would change: each config file, the lines that change, and the skill files. Writes nothing.

all_detected.description: Every agent app found on this computer.

clients.description: Client ids to set up (claude_code, codex, cursor...); empty refreshes the ones already set up.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__setup_uninstall
tools.description: Remove Craft Anything's entries and skill from every agent app's config. Changes other apps' files, so it asks first.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_browser_connect
tools.description: Attach to a loopback CDP endpoint (a browser started with --remote-debugging-port) or launch a located Chromium headless, and report the product, protocol version and debuggable target count. A quick connectivity check before the other browser tools.

cdp_endpoint.description: Loopback CDP endpoint, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:9222. Omit to launch a browser.

launch.description: Launch a located Chromium when no endpoint is given.

no_sandbox.description: Pass --no-sandbox when launching (needed in some containers).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_coverage_measure
tools.description: Turn on V8 precise coverage on one page, observe for a window, then report per-script which functions and block ranges ran (UTF-16 offsets, with call counts when available). Changes the page's profiler state and discards coverage data on stop, so it is not idempotent.

offset.description: First script of the page in the result.

watch_ms.description: How long to let code run while measuring (milliseconds, default 10s).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_listeners_list
tools.description: Resolve a CSS selector on one page and list the DOM event listeners registered on that element: event type, capture/passive/once flags and the handler's script location (URL, line, column). No handler source is read.

selector.description: A CSS selector identifying the element.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_mcp_tools_list
tools.description: Best effort: enable the experimental WebMCP CDP domain and collect any tools the page advertises (names and declared input outlines only) during a short window. The tools are never invoked. Honest when the browser does not support the domain.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_modules_trace
tools.description: Fetch the scripts a live page has loaded and build their ES module import graph: each script and the specifiers it imports, resolved to URLs where relative, with bare specifiers reported as needing an import map. Static reading of the live sources; nothing is executed.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_page_js_analyze
tools.description: Fetch the scripts a live page has loaded over CDP and run the built-in JavaScript analyser on them: chunk graph, module boundaries, routes, HTTP endpoints and vendor fingerprints. Optionally decodes inline (data:) source maps and fetches same-origin maps. Passive; nothing is executed.

load_source_maps.description: Decode inline (data:) source maps and fetch same-origin maps.

offset.description: First module of the page in the result.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_page_screenshot_take
tools.description: Capture a PNG screenshot of the current state of one page and return it inline with its sha256 (plus bytes, dimensions, base64). Passive; the page is not navigated.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_page_show
tools.description: Passively observe one page over CDP for a short window: frame origins, a DOM summary (node names/types and attribute names with value lengths only), parsed scripts (optionally their sources, each with its sha256), resources, and — each opt-in — accessibility names, console entries, network request outlines, WebSocket outlines and storage key names. Never navigates, clicks or evaluates. Cookies, auth headers and storage values are never kept; JSON bodies become outlines.

hidden_values.description: Values to redact wherever they appear (any encoding). Only the count is recorded.

target_id.description: The target id to inspect (from web_pages_list); the first page otherwise.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_page_states_capture
tools.description: On the open website, open up to max_states of its visible menus, pop-ups, tabs and collapsed sections (aria-expanded, aria-haspopup, unselected tabs, <summary>; never form controls or submit buttons) one at a time: click it, take a screenshot, record what changed (expanded, a dialog appeared, the tab or the address changed), then put the page back. Writes state-<n>.png and states.json into a new folder. Clicking runs the site's own code, so it needs your approval.

output_directory.description: Absolute path of a folder that does not exist yet; the states are written there.

width.description: Page width in CSS pixels (320..=3840, default 1440).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_page_watch
tools.description: Passively watch one page over a longer window (default 10s) and record a bounded timeline of network request outlines, console entries, WebSocket frame outlines and navigation/lifecycle events, all data-minimised. Never navigates or evaluates.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_pages_list
tools.description: List the debuggable targets (pages, workers, iframes) of a loopback CDP endpoint with their ids, kinds and origin-only URLs, plus the browser product and protocol version. Read-only discovery over HTTP; no WebSocket.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_pixels_compare
tools.description: Compare two PNG screenshots pixel by pixel with a per-channel threshold (0..255): whether they are comparable, how many pixels differ, the difference fraction, the largest channel delta and the changed bounding box. No pixel data is returned. Pure computation.

before.description: Earlier PNG: a web_page_screenshot_take evidence (inline/retained), or inline {base64} / {path}.

common_area.description:
Compare the area both images share (top-left) when their sizes differ, and add a coarse
`layout_similarity` (0..1, share of 16 px tiles with matching mean colour) and a
`perceptual_similarity` (0..1, mean SSIM of brightness: edges, text, texture). Use it to
compare a rebuild with the original page, whose heights rarely match exactly.

ignore.description:
With common_area: a noise-<width>.png mask from web_site_capture ({path} or {base64});
its white squares (parts that change by themselves) are left out of the layout and detail.

tolerance.description: Per-channel difference a pixel must exceed to count as changed (0..=255).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_recording_show
tools.description: Read a HAR capture offline: requests, methods, statuses, hosts, timings and an API surface grouped by method + origin + path template, with JSON bodies reduced to outlines (no values). Cookies, credential headers, URL user-info and credential-like query values are never kept; secrets the caller names are redacted in raw, URL-encoded and JSON-escaped forms. Paged (offset/limit) or pick entries with record_numbers.

hidden_values.description: Values to redact wherever they appear (tokens, emails, ids). Only their count is recorded.

path.description: Absolute path of the capture file.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_scripts_save
tools.description: Write the scripts held by a web capture (page inspection or walkthrough evidence, a capture JSON file, or a HAR with saved bodies) into a new folder as files/<host>/<path> plus manifest.json; query variants and collisions get content-hash names with a stated reason. The result names the folder to pass to js_app_map.

capture.description: Capture evidence (inline or {"kind":"saved","evidence_id":...}) whose result lists scripts with url and source.

capture_path.description: Or an absolute path to a capture JSON file or a HAR file.

output_directory.description: Absolute path of a folder that does not exist yet.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_site_capture
tools.description: Record the open website into a new folder: full-page PNG screenshots at each requested width, the rendered HTML, design tokens (fonts, sizes, weights, text and background colours as hex, radii, shadows, spacing, content widths, CSS custom properties), the widths its CSS switches layout at, the layout at each width (page width, heading and text sizes, each section's padding, gap, content column and items per row), a layout outline of visible landmarks, headings, controls and images with positions, asset lists (images, stylesheets, scripts, font files, the requests it made), links and form outlines (never values). Writes capture.json and a README.md summary.

max_height.description: Tallest screenshot in CSS pixels; longer pages are cut here (600..=20000, default 12000).

noise_pass.description:
Photograph each width a second time a moment later and save the parts that changed by
themselves (carousels, videos, animations) as noise-<width>.png, white where it changed,
so comparisons can leave them out (default false).

output_directory.description: Absolute path of a folder that does not exist yet; the capture is written there.

widths.description: Page widths to screenshot, in CSS pixels (1..=4 widths, each 320..=3840). Default: desktop and phone.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_site_close
tools.description: Close the private browser started by web_site_open and delete its temporary profile.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_site_open
tools.description: Load a web page (http/https) in a private browser owned by this session (fresh profile, no history or logins) at a chosen window size, wait for it to finish loading, and report its final address, title and size. Every browser tool then inspects this page unless given another endpoint. Runs the site's scripts, so it needs your approval.

headless.description: Run the browser without a window (default true).

height.description: Window height in CSS pixels (320..=4000, default 900).

settle_ms.description: Extra time to let late content settle after the load event, in milliseconds (default 2000).

url.description: The page to open (http or https).

width.description: Window width in CSS pixels (320..=3840, default 1440).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_snapshots_compare
tools.description: Compare two web_page_show captures (frame origins, elements, resources, endpoints and script URLs added or removed), or two web_walkthrough_record runs step by step (steps aligned by step_id, then position: action, status, URL, error and artifact changes; network requests; event counts). normalization lists plain text replacements (e.g. a build id) applied to both sides first. Pure computation over evidence; no browser.

before.description: The earlier capture: web_page_show / web_page_watch evidence (inline or retained).

normalization.description:
Exact-literal replacements applied to every text value of both sides before comparing, in
rule_id order (at most 100), so volatile values such as build ids don't count as changes.

match.description: The exact text to replace (no patterns).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_standin_build
tools.description: Read a network recording (.har) of the original site and write standin.json into a folder: its routes (method and path template, with ids as {id}), and for each the status codes, content types, query names and a bounded set of recorded answers. It's for giving a rebuilt front end something to talk to. Credential headers, cookies and secret-shaped values are dropped and counted; pages, scripts and pictures are left out unless include_static is set. It only knows what was recorded. Returns a summary and a page of routes.

hidden_values.description: Values to drop wherever they appear, in every encoding (emails, ids, tokens). Only their count is recorded.

include_static.description: Also keep pages, scripts, styles, pictures, fonts and media.

only_hosts.description: Only these hosts, e.g. api.example.com (or with a port). Default: every host.

output_dir.description: Absolute path of the folder to write standin.json in (made if missing). An earlier stand-in there is replaced.

path.description: Absolute path of the recording (.har).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_standin_show
tools.description: List the stand-ins running in this session with the requests they answered, and page through the requests that had no recorded answer, most asked first, each with why and the nearest recorded routes. This is how a builder finds out what its front end needs that the recording doesn't have.

id.description: Only this stand-in. Default: every one running.

limit.description: Requests with no answer per page (1–1000).

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_standin_start
tools.description: Answer HTTP requests on this computer from a file written by web_standin_build, and return its URL to point a rebuilt front end at. Listens on 127.0.0.1 only, refuses requests addressed to any other host and pages from other computers, and allows local pages through CORS. Stays running for this session, or until web_standin_stop. A request with no recorded answer gets a 404 with the nearest routes as JSON. Writes replay what was recorded and change nothing. Runs no code from the recording.

path.description: Absolute path of a file written by web_standin_build, or the folder holding it.

port.description: The port to listen on. 0 (the default) picks a free one.

wait.description:
Keep this call going until it's cancelled, then stop and say what was answered. For a one-off
command line, whose session would otherwise end and take the stand-in with it. No other tool
can run in this session meanwhile.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_standin_stop
tools.description: Stop a stand-in started by web_standin_start and free its port: by id, or all of them. With neither, stops the only one running. Returns what it answered.

all.description: Stop every stand-in in this session.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_walkthrough_check
tools.description: Check a script for web_walkthrough_record without running a browser, and list every problem with the step it's in: unknown step kinds, missing fields, selectors CSS doesn't have (XPath, :has-text and the like), locators that aren't exactly one of selector, test_id or role with name, bad settings. Errors are what the recorder would refuse, by the same rules; warnings are what it would run but probably not as meant (a misspelt field it ignores, a repeated step_id). Touches no target.

script.description: What you'd pass to web_walkthrough_record, or only its list of actions.

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__web_walkthrough_record
tools.description: Run a scripted browser session (goto/click/fill/press/select/wait; elements by CSS selector, test_id, or role and accessible name; optional step_id per step) over CDP, attaching to a loopback endpoint or launching a located Chromium. A fixed environment (viewport, locale, time zone, colour scheme, reduced motion, service workers; 1280x720, en-US, UTC, light by default) makes runs repeatable. Captures per-step network request outlines and optional screenshots; keep_bodies can also keep request/response bodies and header values (off by default, credentials and declared secrets redacted). storage can start the run with cookies and local/session storage (values treated as secrets). capture records screenshot, DOM, accessibility tree, history and storage key names after each step and/or at the end. capture.events records console, page errors, WebSockets, frames, workers, popups and (blocked) downloads, each tagged with its step. Executes page interactions and accesses the network, so it needs your approval; declared secrets are redacted in every encoding and bodies are reduced to outlines.

actions.description: The scripted actions, run in order (1..=200).

capture.description: What to record after each step and at the end of the run (besides each step's URL).

capture_network.description: Record network request outlines during the run.

environment.description: Fixed browser settings for the run, so two runs of the same steps see the same page.

hidden_values.description: Values to redact wherever they appear, in every encoding.

keep_bodies.description: Network content to keep besides request outlines (all off by default; needs capture_network).

launch.description: Launch a located Chromium (default when no endpoint is given).

screenshot_each_step.description: Capture a screenshot after each step.

storage.description:
Cookies and storage to start with (e.g. to explore the signed-in side of your own site).
Every value given here is treated as a secret and redacted wherever it shows up.

oneOf.description: The page's HTML, secrets redacted (256 KiB per step, 1 MiB at the end).
Roles and names, as a screen reader sees the page.
The tab's navigation history.
local/session storage key names and cookie names for the current origin (never values).
Console messages (text redacted, capped).
Uncaught exceptions on the page.
WebSocket connections and frames (text frames redacted, capped).
Frames attached, navigated and detached.
Web, shared and service workers started and stopped.
Windows the page opened.
Downloads the page started (they are blocked, never saved).

NetworkContent.description:
Which network values a run keeps. Kept text has declared secrets redacted; credential headers
are always redacted.

url.description: The http(s) URL the cookie belongs to.

events.description: Event families to record over the run, each event tagged with the step it happened in.

WalkthroughEnvironment.description: Viewport, locale, time zone and media settings applied before the first step.

bypass_service_workers.description: Requests skip service workers, so an offline cache can't hide the network.

reduced_motion.description: Ask pages to reduce motion (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce).

timezone.description: IANA time zone, e.g. UTC or Europe/Berlin.

WalkthroughStep.description: One scripted step: an action and, optionally, your name for it (echoed in the result).

oneOf.description:
The element a step acts on: exactly one of a CSS `selector`, a `test_id` (data-testid), or a
`role` with its accessible `name` (what a screen reader says, e.g. role button, name "Sign in").

name.description: The exact accessible name to match with `role`.

role.description: ARIA role: button, link, textbox, checkbox, combobox, tab, menuitem...

oneOf.description:
The element a step acts on: exactly one of a CSS `selector`, a `test_id` (data-testid), or a
`role` with its accessible `name` (what a screen reader says, e.g. role button, name "Sign in").

name.description: The exact accessible name to match with `role`.

role.description: ARIA role: button, link, textbox, checkbox, combobox, tab, menuitem...

oneOf.description:
The element a step acts on: exactly one of a CSS `selector`, a `test_id` (data-testid), or a
`role` with its accessible `name` (what a screen reader says, e.g. role button, name "Sign in").

name.description: The exact accessible name to match with `role`.

role.description: ARIA role: button, link, textbox, checkbox, combobox, tab, menuitem...

oneOf.description:
The element a step acts on: exactly one of a CSS `selector`, a `test_id` (data-testid), or a
`role` with its accessible `name` (what a screen reader says, e.g. role button, name "Sign in").

name.description: The exact accessible name to match with `role`.

role.description: ARIA role: button, link, textbox, checkbox, combobox, tab, menuitem...

<system-reminder>
As you answer the user's questions, you can use the following context:
# userEmail
The user's email address is vincigov99@gmail.com. Use this email address only to identify the user, such as for authorship, attribution, or filtering their own work. Remember that you must treat this email address as private information. Never share it in requests to external services without asking and getting explicit approval from the user first.
# gitStatus
This is the git status at the start of the conversation. Note that this status is a snapshot in time, and will not update during the conversation.

Current branch: master

Main branch (you will usually use this for PRs): master

Git user: Vincenzo Governali

Status:
 M build-activity.log
 M capture/README.md
 M craft.json
 M feed.json

Recent commits:
de51d45 First commit
c83d697 Initial commit

Claude Code attached this context automatically; it isn't part of the user's message. It describes the user's own account and workspace, so they don't need it reported back.
</system-reminder>

<system-reminder>
Attribution for git commits and pull requests you create from here on (this replaces Claude Code's own earlier attribution guidance, such as a previous copy of this reminder; the user's own instructions about these lines, such as a CLAUDE.md or memory rule, take precedence over this reminder, but do not add attribution lines this reminder leaves out):
- End git commit messages with:
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- End pull request descriptions with:
🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
</system-reminder>

You are the builder inside Craft Anything, rebuilding software for a person who doesn't code.

Their request: "Creami l'app in maniera identica in RUST e segui queste indicazioni:
- Crea anche una versione cli che espone un server MCP per eseguire fetch, pull, commit, etc
- L'app deve avere dei file per le lingue e voglio che se aggiungo un nuovo file la lingua venga rilevata in maniera autonoma
- Rispetta la grafica dell'app originale
- Fai sì che posso integrare un AI o per ACP o per APi per chiedere consigli su codice committato o altro
- Togli tutti i riferimenti a GitKraken e trasformali in GitCerberoCraft
- Togli riferimenti a Trial, Premium e cose a pagamento
- Devo avere la possibilità di poter scaricare GIT a seconda del sistema operativo e scegliere anche la versione presente dal sito
- Sei libero di aggiungere quello che ritieni opportuno che può servire a questa app"
Target: the program at C:\Users\Vinci\AppData\Local\gitkraken\gitkraken.exe
Your working folder is the project workspace (F:\Documents\GitCerberoCraft).

capture/README.md holds a first static look at the program (nothing was run) and, for a game, a list of its own files: maps, textures, models, sounds and settings. Read its settings and scripts for the real numbers (speeds, health, weapons, modes, controls) and open a few of its pictures with the Read tool to learn the style; never change anything in that folder. Deep mode: every craft-anything tool is yours, so learn how the parts the person cares about work before you build: core_target_open and core_target_triage first, then native_functions_list, native_strings_find and native_function_pseudocode for a program's code, managed_assembly_show and managed_members_list for .NET, java_* and android_* for Java and Android apps, js_app_map, js_sources_restore and js_electron_* for an Electron app, and game_archives_list and the other game_* tools for a game's files.

What to build: a playable game that plays like the original: the same rules, controls, numbers and feel.

How to build it, unless their request says otherwise: Use Rust with macroquad (a small game library). Create a cargo project in app/ itself (app/Cargo.toml and app/src/main.rs, not a folder inside app/), keep assets procedural (shapes, colours) unless the person provides some, and run `cargo build` until it succeeds.

How to work: you lead the investigation and the craft-anything tools answer your questions with evidence.
1) Study the evidence, overview first (the README and summaries before the details). Where it leaves a gap that matters to the result, ask a focused follow-up with the craft-anything tools instead of guessing: capture another width or an opened state into a new folder under checks/, inspect a page or a bundle, look up a program's strings or functions by their exact names, read a game's settings or files. Don't repeat a call that already answered. Record each question the evidence doesn't answer yet with core_unknown_add (the question, what would settle it as probes, and how much it matters as severity), and when a later look answers it, close it with core_unknown_edit (status resolved, the resolution and the evidence ids that settle it); until then say in it what you did instead (an estimate, a placeholder or a question for the person). Missing evidence is never proof, so mark what you estimated.
2) Make a short checklist with TodoWrite: 3-7 steps in plain words the person can follow (no file names or jargon), each with a short activeForm such as "Drawing the map"; the person watches it live, so keep it updated as you go.
3) Build it in app/ and fix errors until the build succeeds.
4) Test it against the original with rebuild_check: it runs the same checks Craft Anything runs after your turn and lists what differs and what couldn't be compared. Fix the results it says another builder turn can resolve, then build and check again. When it says another builder turn cannot resolve a comparison, stop retrying that comparison, keep it unverified and state the limit in your reply.
5) Before you reply, go through your checklist and core_unknowns_show once more: settle what one more look can settle, and say what's left in your summary.

Rules:
- Their request comes first. When it says how to build (a language, framework, engine, library or platform), build with exactly that, even where these instructions name something else: the stack given here is only the default for what the request leaves open. Don't switch away from what they asked for to get past a failing build or check; fix the build instead.
- Change files only inside app/. Everything else in the workspace is read-only evidence.
- Rebuild the layout, styling and behaviour yourself from the evidence. Don't copy logos, photos, brand names or long passages of text unless the person confirms they own the original or have permission (ask once with core_person_ask if it matters); otherwise use neutral placeholders: simple shapes or gradients for images, short sample copy for text.
- Use the core_person_ask tool (craft-anything MCP server) only for choices that really change the result. Give 2-4 short choices. Never ask about technical details you can decide yourself.
- Build what the person asked for. If part of it won't fit this version (for example online co-op, a whole game mode or another platform), ask with core_person_ask before leaving it out, with the smaller version as one of the choices; never drop it silently.
- Never start dev servers, watchers or anything that doesn't exit (npm run dev, npm start, vite, cargo watch). Craft Anything serves and checks the build itself.
- Finish with 3-5 plain sentences for the person: what you built, what differs from the original or is still unknown, and one idea for what to ask next. No code and no file paths in that summary.

Making it play like the original:
- Start app/MECHANICS.md: every number that shapes how it plays. Movement (walk and run speed, acceleration, friction, air control, jump height, gravity, crouch), camera (field of view, mouse sensitivity), each weapon (damage, fire rate, magazine, reload time, spread, recoil, range), health and armour, respawn, scoring, modes, timers, and how computer players behave. Next to each value say where it came from (a file in the game's folder, a function address or evidence id) or mark it "estimated". Build from that sheet and keep it up to date.
- Match the controls and key bindings, the on-screen information and where it sits, and the rules of each mode.
- Keep the same values in app/mechanics.json, which Craft Anything reads after each build: {"version": 1, "values": [{"name": "walk speed", "group": "movement", "value": 4.5, "unit": "m/s", "source": "function 0x140012a0"}, {"name": "crouch", "group": "controls", "value": "hold", "estimated": true}]}. A value is a number, text or true/false; give each one its source or "estimated": true, and implement the sheet's behavior. Equivalent calculations and unit conversions are allowed. tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 28800000ms / 480 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 14400000ms (240 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. With `run_in_background` the timeout is instead how long the command may run in the background (default 14400000ms / 240 minutes, max 28800000ms / 8 hours); at that limit it is stopped and you are notified.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__app_builds_line_up
tools.description: Pair the functions of two builds of a program (two absolute paths) with the built-in engine. In order: unique names that aren't generated; Rust names with the compiler's hashes left out (a crate's hash changes with the toolchain); identical bytes; bytes with addresses masked out; a structural fingerprint of block count, called names and referenced strings. Each pair says how it was matched, with what confidence, and what comparing the bodies found: a pair by name is still reported as changed when its code differs. Candidates that can't be told apart stay unpaired and are listed as ambiguous. Lists are paged together (offset/limit); show picks one; detail=summary keeps every row for core_evidence_browse. Nothing is executed. Takes as long as analysing both programs.

Each pair says how it was matched, with what confidence, and what comparing the bodies found: a pair by name is still reported as changed when its code differs. Candidates that can't be told apart stay unpaired and are listed as ambiguous. Lists are paged together (offset/limit); show picks one; detail=summary keeps every row for core_evidence_browse. tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__app_folder_explain
tools.description: Survey an installed app's folder (absolute path; a macOS .app or its Contents, a Windows or Linux install folder) when you don't know what it is. Walks the folder within max_entries and max_depth, following no links, running nothing and writing nothing, and reads only the first and last 4 KiB of the files that need a look, plus a search of up to 64 MiB of up to 4 main programs for Tauri's own text, to name the runtimes it may be built on: Electron, Tauri, CEF, Qt, Flutter, .NET, Java, Python (with PyInstaller), Node, Unity, Unreal, Godot, other game engines, or plain native code. Each candidate has a strength and the files that support it, and next_steps says which tool to run on which file. These are inferences: a file being there doesn't prove the app runs it.

tools.description: Make a game-ready, low-poly 3D model (GLB) with fal.ai (Tripo P1) and save it inside app/. Give a prompt (a picture is made first, then turned into the model) or an image (a web address, or a picture inside the project such as reference/picture-1.png). faces caps the face count (48 to 20000, default 3000): about 500-1500 for small props and pickups, 2000-5000 for weapons, furniture and vehicles, 6000-15000 for main characters; fewer faces run faster, so use the fewest that still look right. textured (default true) gives colours and surfaces. A textured model costs $0.50 plus $0.15 for the picture, counted against the project's asset budget; it takes a minute or two. Describe one original object per model; never ask for recognisable characters, logos or brand artwork. Returns where it was saved, the cost and the budget left.

Commands are checked against an allow-list of read-only families: information (i...), printing and disassembly (p..., x...), analysis (a...), search (/...), seek (s...), flags (f...), comments (C...), types (t...) and help (?...). Shell escapes, writes, file opening, debugging, scripts, configuration changes, pipes, redirects and command chaining are refused. Returns the raw text paged by lines. Optional engine.

tools.name: mcp__craft-anything__native_rizin_session_begin
tools.description: Start Rizin's debugger (user settings and scripts off, no prompt or colours) on a program (absolute path, optional arguments), which it starts stopped before its first instruction, or attach it to a running process by pid. Returns a session_id for native_rizin_session_command_run, native_rizin_session_show and native_rizin_session_end, plus Rizin's start-up messages. The program's own console output isn't captured. Sessions live in memory for this run; at most 4 at a time. Starting a program or attaching to one asks for consent.

A command still running at the deadline (a `dc` that never stops) keeps running and the next command waits for it. Visual mode isn't available. Commands can run the program and change its memory, so this asks for consent.

tools.description: Summarize a saved pcap or pcapng capture with the built-in decoder (nothing installed): format, interfaces and link types, packet and byte counts, time span, frames per protocol, busiest addresses, conversations (flows) with packets and bytes in each direction and the application protocols seen (paged), DNS questions and answers, HTTP/1.x requests (method, Host, target; credentials removed) and TLS ClientHello server names (SNI) and ALPN. Bounded by time, output and files; the whole process group is killed on timeout or cancel. Runs code, so it needs your OK.

content.text:
Ho trovato e corretto il motivo del 403. Quando Git è installato, l'app non passava mai a Git il token salvato nelle Preferenze. Git usava quindi la password ricordata da Windows, che spesso appartiene a un altro account. Anche dopo aver cambiato il token, quello nuovo veniva usato solo al riavvio dell'app.

Ora il token salvato viene sempre usato per push, pull e fetch su GitHub e GitLab, e vale subito dopo averlo incollato. Per quel sito l'app salta le password ricordate da Windows, così si usa sempre l'account giusto. Ho provato che Git riceve davvero il token, ma non ho potuto provare un push vero sul tuo account, quindi non so ancora quale fosse la causa esatta nel tuo caso.

Se GitHub rifiuta ancora il push, l'app spiega il motivo in italiano invece di mostrare solo "403". Per esempio: il token appartiene a un altro utente, gli manca il permesso "repo", è un token "fine-grained" che non include quel repository, oppure l'organizzazione richiede l'autorizzazione SSO. Il messaggio resta a schermo abbastanza a lungo da poterlo leggere e si chiude con un clic. In Preferenze > Integrazioni c'è anche un pulsante "Prova token" che dice a quale account appartiene il token.

Sotto il pulsante verde di Commit c'è un nuovo pulsante "Commit e push", visibile nella foto di prova. Fa il commit e subito dopo il push del branch. La stessa possibilità è nella versione a riga di comando e nel server MCP. Compilazione e prova automatica sono andate a buon fine.

Prova a fare di nuovo il push: se fallisce ancora, mandami il messaggio di spiegazione e sistemiamo il token di conseguenza.
